mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in over 40% of periods following a FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in over 60% of periods after UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in over 40% of periods with rising HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production signals reduced supply, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in over 50% of periods after INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth and rising unemployment indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate decelerates and UNRATE increases
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in over 50% of periods with slowing GDP and rising UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher FEDFUNDS rates increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in over 40% of periods with high FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing non-farm employment suggests economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in over 30% of periods after PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPI and increasing FEDFUNDS indicate inflationary pressures and tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in over 50% of periods with rising CPI and FEDFUNDS.
